passages.note: Roll call shows Mathis voting No on final passage of HB2853 (2022), the ESA expansion bill, 31-26.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Enacted text (Chapter 388) opens ESA eligibility to nearly all Arizona students notwithstanding prior qualifying criteria, matching rung 5's universal-eligibility clause.

rows.reasoning: Mathis voted No on HB2853 (2022), a single-subject ESA bill whose operative text (15-2401.01) made nearly every Arizona K-12 and qualifying preschool student eligible 'notwithstanding' prior criteria, matching rung 5's 'universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school.' Per the annex's own hard case, a No vote on an expansion bill alone is only direction-only: it shows opposition to the expansion but does not separate rung 1 ('eliminating voucher programs') from rung 2 ('opposing voucher programs and blocking their expansion, without moving to eliminate existing ones').
needs_source: Mathis's own words on HB2853 or on the existing Arizona ESA program, to distinguish eliminating existing voucher programs (rung 1) from opposing expansion without repeal (rung 2).
